title: Refit a desktop arm's parallel link on the closure branch that keeps its wrist level
instruction: Fit the grey parallel link onto the red pin so the yellow arm's blue wrist plate sits level, then let go.
context: Robotics technicians, electromechanical assemblers, industrial electronics repairers and machinery mechanics (O*NET 17-3024.01, 51-2023, 49-2094, 49-9041) refit the passive parallel link that keeps the wrist of a desktop parallelogram arm level, after a motor, bearing or link swap; palletizing robots use the same four-bar at about ten times the size. A pinned four-bar closes two ways: as a parallelogram, which holds the wrist level, or crossed, which locks it off level. With the link off, the wrist hangs in the crossed pose, so pinning the link where it hangs closes the wrong branch. Unlike turn-and-pin tasks, nothing says to turn the plate and there is no mark or hole to find: the link clicks shut either way, and the skill is choosing which way the loop closes.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. A bench model of a desktop parallelogram arm's level-keeping four-bar (110 mm links) stands in a vertical plane facing the robot (every hinge axis points at the robot). (1) Base: grey steel, sRGB (0.42, 0.43, 0.45), 1.5 kg, fixed to the table: a back block 22 x 90 x 112 mm (x, y, z) centred at (0.339, -0.025, 0.804), a post 20 x 24 x 110 mm centred at (0.318, -0.053, 0.803) and a foot plate 52 x 120 x 8 mm centred at (0.334, -0.025, 0.752). The arm pivot A is at (0.320, 0.000, 0.848). (2) Red pin: steel, sRGB (0.85, 0.10, 0.10), part of the base, 8 mm diameter, axis along x at (y -0.053, z 0.848), sticking out of the post from x 0.308 to 0.284 (24 mm), 53 mm to the robot's right of A at the same height. (3) Upper arm: yellow aluminium, sRGB (0.95, 0.72, 0.10), 126 x 16 x 12 mm, 80 g, on pivot A, held by its brake at 65 deg above horizontal reaching up and to the robot's left; its tip pivot C is at (0.320, 0.046, 0.947), 110 mm from A. (4) Wrist plate: blue aluminium, sRGB (0.15, 0.35, 0.80), 122 x 20 x 10 mm bar, 66 g, balanced on pivot C at its middle, in the layer 8 to 18 mm in front of the arm (x 0.312 to 0.302); its rear pin D is 53 mm from C. At reset it stands on end: rear end down, D at (0.307, 0.046, 0.894). Level means its long axis horizontal with D pointing to the robot's right. (5) Parallel link: grey aluminium, sRGB (0.72, 0.74, 0.77), 110 mm pin to pin (135 mm overall), 12 x 8 mm section, 40 g, in the layer 21 to 29 mm in front of the arm (x 0.299 to 0.291), pinned to the plate at D and hanging straight down from it at reset (eye centre near (0.295, 0.049, 0.784)). Its free end is a snap eye: a 10 x 14 mm pocket whose mouth faces the side that leads when the link swings toward the pin, closed by (6) a sprung tongue: black steel, sRGB (0.12, 0.12, 0.13), 3 g, 16.5 x 8 x 8 mm with a 45 deg lead-in, sliding 10 mm along the link on a 40 N/m spring (0.12 N preload). The pin pushes it back and it clicks shut behind the pin. Friction: pin, eye and tongue 0.15 static / 0.10 dynamic; link 0.3 / 0.25; plate 0.6 / 0.5.
scoring: Measured from link poses every control step from reset: the plate's tilt from level (deg), the upper arm's angle, the pin's centre in the eye (mm along and across the link) and the tongue's retraction. Snapped: pin centre inside the pocket (-1.0 to +1.8 mm along the link, within 3.3 mm across it) with the tongue back within 1 mm of its stop. Level: tilt within 3 deg. Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step and cleared only by the simulator reset, so unclipping and starting again never clears it). Gate, any time in the run, gives 0: the upper arm forced 1.5 deg or more off its braked 65 deg. Ladder: 0.25 = at some time the plate level while the pocket centre was within 10 mm of the pin; 0.5 = at some time snapped with the plate level; 0.75 = at the end snapped with the plate level; 1.0 = 0.75, the plate still (under 3 mm/s and 3 deg/s, from its pose change between control steps) for the last 1 s, and the release gate: every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the base, arm, plate, link and tongue and both grippers moving under 5 mm/s for the last 1 s. A snap on the crossed closure leaves the plate 90 deg off level and earns nothing. Success (1.0) must hold 1 s. Real trial: a protractor or a top photo for the plate tilt and the arm angle; the snap is visible and audible.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Press the eye's tongue back with a finger and lift the link off the red pin. Let the link hang from the plate: the plate turns under it until its rear end points straight down and the link hangs vertical. Check with a protractor that the arm still sits at 65 deg on its brake. The base is bolted on taped outlines and needs no reset.
fidelity: Desktop-arm scale (110 mm links); a palletizer's level-keeping four-bar is about ten times larger. The upper arm's brake is a stiff PD hold (200 N m/rad), the plate is balanced on its pivot, the hinges are frictionless, and the snap eye is rigid contact geometry with a sprung sliding tongue (40 N/m) standing in for a spring clip. The links sit in separate layers, so they can pass each other. The eye's 1 mm play along the link leaves the plate 0.8 deg off level at rest.
